judged_by: Matched by a Claude Opus 5.5 agent on 2026-11-25; not yet checked by the labeler.

central_claim.note: Both halves: conservatives in liberal climates less hesitant and more often boosted; liberals less hesitant regardless. 'Moderates' is the paper's own framing.

evidence.note: Online survey via Qualtrics Panels, March 8 to April 19, 2023 (E1; 'convenience' not said, wording leniency as in earlier matches). N = 683 without the 1,777/970 screening figures (E2 partial). 'Quota-based sample of White and Black participants across income levels' gives the race and income quotas without the four groups or the median split (E7 partial).
Two self-rated items (social, economic) on an 11-point scale; averaging not said, counted as E4. Percent Republican 2020 vote by zip code (E3).
Linear and logistic regressions with the interaction term and the full control list.

key_findings.note: Steeper rise of hesitancy with conservatism in conservative climates; the liberals-regardless half is in [4].
Booster hesitancy interaction significant with 'a similar pattern' (p.7, p.10): accurate, but no gold finding covers booster hesitancy alone (as in earlier matches).
Conservative half of F3 with 60% vs under 35%; the liberals-boosted-anywhere half is not stated in the slot.

flags.text: Says conservatives' hesitancy 'was influenced by' their regional political climate. The paper reports an association (abstract: 'conservatives' likelihood was associated with their political climate') and says it 'cannot assume causal or directional associations' (p.10).

key_findings.note: Liberals low regardless of climate; conservatives' hesitancy depends on climate. Completes F2 with [0].

scope_and_limits.note: Other zip-code differences such as population density (L1). Effect modification not tested is named without its consequence (L5 partial).
'Influences' wording not flagged, following the earlier match of the same phrasing.

theoretical_positioning.note: Both literatures and the extension by testing their interaction. 'Prior studies had not addressed' is true to the paper's 'first assessment' (p.7).
Consistent with the two prior literatures (p.10); the novel-interaction part repeats T2 from [0].
